title: Past simple + prepositions of place + question words
title_it: Past simple + preposizioni di luogo + parole interrogative
goal: Talk about finished past actions, say where things are, and ask questions with where, when, who, why, which and whose.
goal_it: Parlare di azioni passate finite, dire dove sono le cose e fare domande con where, when, who, why, which e whose.

steps.title: Past simple: finished actions
en: We use the past simple for finished actions at a definite time in the past: yesterday, last week, three days ago, in 2019, when I was a child.
Regular verbs add -ed (work, worked). Spelling: live, lived; stop, stopped; study, studied. Irregular verbs have their own past form and you must learn them.
it: Usiamo il past simple per azioni finite in un momento preciso del passato: yesterday, last week, three days ago, in 2019, when I was a child.
I verbi regolari aggiungono -ed (work, worked). Ortografia: live, lived; stop, stopped; study, studied. I verbi irregolari hanno una forma propria da imparare.

examples.en: We went to Bath last weekend.
examples.it: Siamo andati a Bath lo scorso fine settimana.

examples.en: She bought a new coat yesterday.
examples.it: Ieri ha comprato un cappotto nuovo.

examples.en: They watched a film and ate pizza.
examples.it: Hanno guardato un film e mangiato pizza.

steps.title: Past simple: negative, questions and was / were
steps.title_it: Past simple: negativa, domande e was / were
en: Negative: didn't (did not) + base verb. Question: Did + subject + base verb. After did / didn't the verb does NOT change: Did you go? (not Did you went?).
The past of be is was / were: I was, you were, he / she / it was, we / they were. Negative: wasn't, weren't. Questions: Was she tired? Were they late? No did with be.
Do is also a normal verb: What did you do? I didn't do anything.
it: Negativa: didn't (did not) + verbo base. Domanda: Did + soggetto + verbo base. Dopo did / didn't il verbo NON cambia: Did you go? (non Did you went?).
Il passato di be è was / were: I was, you were, he / she / it was, we / they were. Negativa: wasn't, weren't. Domande: Was she tired? Were they late? Con be non serve did.
Do è anche un verbo normale: What did you do? I didn't do anything.

examples.en: Did you enjoy the concert? No, I didn't.
examples.it: Ti è piaciuto il concerto? No.

examples.en: I didn't buy anything at the market.
examples.it: Non ho comprato niente al mercato.

examples.en: Were your parents at home last night?
examples.it: I tuoi genitori erano a casa ieri sera?

steps.title: Prepositions of place: in / on / at and the room
steps.title_it: Preposizioni di luogo: in / on / at e la stanza
en: In = inside a space or a town. On = on a surface, a street or a floor. At = a precise point. Then learn the useful words for describing where things are in a room. In these examples we use there is / there are: you already know them.
it: In = dentro uno spazio o una città. On = su una superficie, una strada o un piano. At = un punto preciso. Poi impara le parole utili per descrivere dove sono le cose in una stanza. In questi esempi usiamo there is / there are: li conosci già.

head: Preposition
Meaning
Example
rows: There is a lamp in the room. I live in Leeds.
su, a contatto, su una strada o un piano
The pen is on the table. The flat is on the second floor.
I'm at the door. We wait at the bus stop.
The pen fell onto the floor.
There is a light over the table. A picture is above the bed.
The cat is under the chair.
The clock is below the window.
The lamp is between the sofa and the window.
There is a bag behind the door. A bike is in front of the house.
The bank is opposite the station.
He ran into the room and out of the kitchen.
I walk to work from home.
The shop is next to the bank and close to the park.

examples.en: There are three pictures on the wall.
examples.it: Ci sono tre quadri sulla parete.

examples.en: Is there a chair between the table and the door?
examples.it: C'è una sedia tra il tavolo e la porta?

examples.en: The ceiling light is over the table.
examples.it: La luce del soffitto è sopra il tavolo.

steps.title: Question words 1: where, when, who, why, which, whose
steps.title_it: Parole interrogative 1: where, when, who, why, which, whose
en: Order of a question: question word + auxiliary + subject + verb. Nothing goes before the question word, and the preposition goes at the end: Who are you talking to? (not To who ...).
When who is the subject, there is no do / did: Who called you? Why is answered with because. Which = quale (a limited choice). Whose = di chi.
it: Ordine della domanda: parola interrogativa + ausiliare + soggetto + verbo. Davanti alla parola interrogativa non va nulla e la preposizione va in fondo: Who are you talking to? (non To who ...).
Quando who è il soggetto non serve do / did: Who called you? A why si risponde con because. Which = quale (scelta limitata). Whose = di chi.

head: Word
Meaning
Example
rows: Where do you usually go? / Where are you going? / Where did you go yesterday? / Where have you been?
Who did you meet? Who called you?
Why were you late? Because the bus was late.
Which bus do you take, the 12 or the 15?
Whose pen is this? It's Maria's.

examples.en: Whose bag is on the chair?
examples.it: Di chi è la borsa sulla sedia?

steps.q: We ___ to the cinema last night.
steps.q_it: Siamo andati al cinema ieri sera.
steps.why: Last night is a finished time, so we use the past simple. Go is irregular: went.
steps.why_it: Last night è un tempo finito, quindi past simple. Go è irregolare: went.

steps.q: Last weekend I ___ (visit) my grandparents.
steps.q_it: Lo scorso fine settimana ho fatto visita ai nonni.
steps.why: Regular verb in the past simple: visit + ed.
steps.why_it: Verbo regolare al past simple: visit + ed.

steps.q: Tom ___ (not / buy) anything at the market yesterday.
steps.q_it: Tom non ha comprato niente al mercato ieri.
steps.why: Negative past simple: didn't + base verb (buy, not bought).
steps.why_it: Negativa del past simple: didn't + verbo base (buy, non bought).

steps.q: My parents ___ (be) in Rome in 2015.
steps.q_it: I miei genitori erano a Roma nel 2015.
steps.why: In 2015 is a finished time. Past of be with they: were.
steps.why_it: In 2015 è un tempo finito. Passato di be con they: were.

steps.q: Every day she gets up at seven. Yesterday she ___ (get) up at seven.
steps.q_it: Ogni giorno si alza alle sette. Ieri si è alzata alle sette.
steps.why: Yesterday asks for the past simple. Get is irregular: got.
steps.why_it: Yesterday vuole il past simple. Get è irregolare: got.

steps.q: ___ you enjoy the party on Saturday?
steps.q_it: Ti è piaciuta la festa di sabato?
steps.why: Enjoy is a normal verb in the past, so the question starts with Did.
steps.why_it: Enjoy è un verbo normale al passato, quindi la domanda inizia con Did.

steps.q: Did you ___ (see) the new film?
steps.q_it: Hai visto il nuovo film?
steps.hint: after did the verb stays in the base form
steps.why: After Did the verb is in the base form: see, not saw.
steps.why_it: Dopo Did il verbo è alla forma base: see, non saw.

steps.q: Put the words in order.
steps.q_it: Metti le parole in ordine.
steps.why: Subject + didn't + base verb. Do is the main verb here.
steps.why_it: Soggetto + didn't + verbo base. Qui do è il verbo principale.

steps.q: The lamp is ___ the table. It does not touch it.
steps.q_it: La lampada è sopra il tavolo. Non lo tocca.
steps.why: Over means above without touching. On means touching the surface.
steps.why_it: Over significa sopra senza toccare. On significa a contatto con la superficie.

steps.q: Meet me ___ the bus stop at eight.
steps.q_it: Ci vediamo alla fermata dell'autobus alle otto.
steps.why: The bus stop is a precise point: at.
steps.why_it: La fermata è un punto preciso: at.

steps.q: There are three pictures ___ the wall.
steps.q_it: Ci sono tre quadri sulla parete.
steps.why: A wall is a surface: on the wall.
steps.why_it: Una parete è una superficie: on the wall.

steps.q: The cat is sleeping ___ the chair, on the floor.
steps.q_it: Il gatto dorme sotto la sedia, sul pavimento.
steps.why: Under means below something, covered by it.
steps.why_it: Under significa sotto qualcosa, coperto da esso.

steps.q: There isn't a TV ___ the bedroom.
steps.q_it: Non c'è una TV in camera da letto.
steps.why: A room is a space: in the bedroom.
steps.why_it: Una stanza è uno spazio: in the bedroom.

steps.q: Describe the room.
steps.q_it: Descrivi la stanza.
answers: There is a lamp between the sofa and the window
steps.why: There is + a + noun + between + A and B.
steps.why_it: There is + a + nome + between + A e B.

steps.q: ___ is your birthday? On the fourth of May.
steps.q_it: Quando è il tuo compleanno? Il quattro maggio.
steps.why: The answer is a date, so we ask with When.
steps.why_it: La risposta è una data, quindi chiediamo con When.

steps.q: ___ bus do you take to work, the 12 or the 15?
steps.q_it: Quale autobus prendi per andare al lavoro, il 12 o il 15?
steps.why: Which is used for a limited choice (the 12 or the 15).
steps.why_it: Which si usa per una scelta limitata (il 12 o il 15).

steps.q: A: ___ did you leave early? B: Because I was tired.
steps.q_it: A: Perché sei andato via presto? B: Perché ero stanco.
steps.why: Because answers a Why question.
steps.why_it: Because risponde a una domanda con Why.

steps.q: Who are you talking ___?
steps.q_it: Con chi stai parlando?
steps.hint: the preposition goes at the end
steps.why: The preposition goes at the end of the question: Who are you talking to?
steps.why_it: La preposizione va in fondo alla domanda: Who are you talking to?

steps.q: Make a question.
steps.q_it: Forma una domanda.
steps.why: Question word + did + subject + base verb. Yesterday needs the past simple.
steps.why_it: Parola interrogativa + did + soggetto + verbo base. Yesterday richiede il past simple.

steps.q: Who ___ you this morning? (call)
steps.q_it: Chi ti ha chiamato stamattina?
steps.hint: who is the subject: no did
steps.why: When Who is the subject we do not use did: Who called you?
steps.why_it: Quando Who è il soggetto non si usa did: Who called you?

steps.q: A: ___ ? B: I went to the dentist yesterday.
steps.q_it: A: ___ ? B: Sono andato dal dentista ieri.
steps.why: Yesterday is a finished time, so the question uses did + base verb: go.
steps.why_it: Yesterday è un tempo finito, quindi la domanda usa did + verbo base: go.

steps.q: Make a question.
steps.q_it: Forma una domanda.
answers: Why did you stay at home last night
steps.why: Why + did + subject + base verb. Last night is a finished time.
steps.why_it: Why + did + soggetto + verbo base. Last night è un tempo finito.

steps.q: Which question goes with the word now?
steps.q_it: Quale domanda va con la parola now?
steps.why: Now means this moment, so we use the present continuous: are you going.
steps.why_it: Now indica questo momento, quindi present continuous: are you going.

steps.q: Look! The children ___ in the garden.
steps.q_it: Guarda! I bambini stanno giocando in giardino.
steps.why: Look! shows an action happening now: present continuous.
steps.why_it: Look! indica un'azione che accade adesso: present continuous.

steps.q: My brother usually ___ (get) up at six, but today he is still in bed.
steps.q_it: Mio fratello di solito si alza alle sei, ma oggi è ancora a letto.
steps.why: Usually shows a routine: present simple, with -s for he.
steps.why_it: Usually indica una routine: present simple, con -s per he.

steps.q: Hurry up! The bus ___ (come).
steps.q_it: Sbrigati! Sta arrivando l'autobus.
steps.why: Hurry up! means now: present continuous (is coming).
steps.why_it: Hurry up! significa adesso: present continuous (is coming).

cards.ex: There is a light on the ceiling.
The cat is on the floor.
There is a picture on the wall.
The lamp is between the sofa and the window.
The bank is opposite the station.
A bike is in front of the door and a bag is behind it.
I went to town and bought a pen.
I didn't go out last night.
